items.title: BBC reveals its emergency radio plan for a national blackout
items.summary: The BBC has a 'Black Sky' plan to keep broadcasting on FM radio for at least 72 hours if the power fails nationwide. The government says there is no specific threat to the grid.

items.title: Low wind triggers a grid warning for tight supplies
items.summary: The grid operator NESO warned supplies would be tight on Monday 9 November as weak winds cut generation, then cancelled the notice. It is the seventh such warning this year, against one in 2025.

items.title: 1,200 homes lose power after a lorry hits a power line in North Devon
items.summary: A lorry's crane struck an 11kV overhead line near the A361 at Ashford and caught fire. National Grid restored all 1,205 properties by about 9pm.

items.title: Economist questions whether the lights will stay on this winter
items.summary: Oxford professor Sir Dieter Helm says relying on wind leaves Britain exposed in winter and calls for more backup power and storage. NESO says supplies will be secure.

items.title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 homes without power
items.summary: Around 160,000 homes lost power at the peak and two men were killed by falling trees. About 90,000 were still off supply that evening.

items.title: Storm Austen cuts power to 16,000 homes in the South West
items.summary: Dozens of schools in Cornwall opened late or stayed shut. National Grid said it had restored more than 12,000 properties by 8am on the Friday.

items.title: Winter blackout risk rises for the first time since 2022
items.summary: NESO's winter outlook puts Britain's spare margin at 5.9GW, down from 6.1GW last year, though it still expects supplies to stay secure.
